## TL;DR

**The community has consolidated on one successor: [caozhiyuan/copilot-api](https://github.com/caozhiyuan/copilot-api)** (npm `@jeffreycao/copilot-api`). Issue [#233](https://github.com/ericc-ch/copilot-api/issues/233) in the original repo officially points to it. I ran it locally on port 4142 and verified: **extended thinking returns real thinking blocks, WebSearch actually works (returned Node.js LTS v24.18.0 with source links), tool round-trips are native-passthrough**, and hyphenated model ids are normalized. It's the clear best practice.

Bonus discovery while testing: **Claude Code currently lets `settings.local.json` env override shell env vars** — my first fork test silently went to your 4141 proxy because your repo has `copilot-here on` active. This contradicts third-party docs and slightly weakens our Layer-1 wrapper (details below).

## Fork landscape (all candidates, verified via npm + GitHub)

| Fork / npm package | Version | Downloads/mo | Last release | Key approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`@jeffreycao/copilot-api`** (caozhiyuan, 891 stars) | 1.13.14 | 19,552 | 2026-07-01 (near-daily) | Native Anthropic `/v1/messages` passthrough + Responses-API WebSearch + dashboard |
| `copilot-api-node20` (johnib) | 0.37.1 | 3,706 | 2026-07-02 | Native `/v1/messages` passthrough for Claude (created specifically to fix the tool-loop bug [#46](https://github.com/ericc-ch/copilot-api/issues/46)) |
| `@hsupu/copilot-api` (puxu-msft/copilot-api-js) | 0.8.2 | 1,593 | 2026-06-30 | OpenAI+Anthropic+AOAI+Gemini endpoints, `opus[1m]` aliases |
| `betahi-copilot-api` ([#240](https://github.com/ericc-ch/copilot-api/issues/240)) | 0.7.5 | 100 | 2026-04-27 | Reasoning-effort control (`COPILOT_REASONING_EFFORT`); semi-stale |
| `copilot-api` (ericc-ch, original — what you run) | 0.7.0 | 3,597 | 2025-10-05, **dead** | Anthropic→OpenAI→Anthropic translation (the root cause of most gaps) |

The winner's issue tracker is remarkably responsive — feature requests filed and closed within a day (HTTPS, startup smoke-test, Tavily/Exa search grounding, all closed 2026-07-01), and the `context_management` regression ([#305](https://github.com/caozhiyuan/copilot-api/issues/305)) gets maintainer replies same-day.

## What I verified live (fork v1.13.14, port 4142, your token)

- **Thinking blocks: fixed.** `thinking: enabled` returned `["thinking","text"]` content with `thinking_tokens: 138` in usage — v0.7.0 silently dropped these. It routes Claude traffic to Copilot's native Anthropic endpoint (your account is Copilot Enterprise: `api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com/v1/messages`).
- **WebSearch: fixed.** Real headless Claude Code run: "1 search performed, Node.js LTS is v24.18.0" with nodejs.org citations. It routes WebSearch through a Responses-capable GPT model (default config `messageApiWebSearchModel: "gpt-5-mini"`, already enabled out of the box). Caveat: my raw-API probe hit one transient 500 in the same route, so treat it as working-but-occasionally-flaky.
- **Tool use: native round-trip works**; this architecture eliminates the translation-mangling class of bugs behind the infinite tool-retry loops in the original.
- **Hyphenated ids (`claude-haiku-4-5`): accepted** — the Claude Code 2.1.x compatibility issue is gone, and cache/usage fields are properly reported (`cache_creation`, `cache_read_input_tokens`).
- **Known wart:** injecting `context_management` (newer Claude Code context-editing) gets a 400 from Copilot's native endpoint ([#305](https://github.com/caozhiyuan/copilot-api/issues/305), version-dependent). Real Claude Code runs in my tests didn't trigger it, but it's the one issue to watch.

## Best practice if you switch

1. `COPILOT_API_PKG` can't just be swapped — the fork's `start` has **no `--rate-limit`/`--wait` flags** (I read its `src/start.ts`), so `copilot-proxy start` needs a small adjustment. It also has no rate limiting at all; the README's mitigation is reducing chatter instead: `CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0` (also prevents prompt-cache invalidation), `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION=false`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AWAY_SUMMARY=0` — worth adding to `copilot-here`/`copilot-run` env regardless.
2. It reuses the same `~/.local/share/copilot-api/github_token`, so no re-auth needed (verified — it booted straight into the model list), and it bundles the usage dashboard locally (`/usage-viewer`).
3. `bunx @jeffreycao/copilot-api@<pin> start --port 4141` works today as a manual trial.

## One finding that affects our own design

The empirical precedence in current Claude Code is: **`.claude/settings.local.json` env beats inherited shell env** (my `env ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=4142 claude ...` run from this repo was served by 4141 until I moved to a neutral directory). Practical consequence: `claude-copilot` cannot override a project where `copilot-here on` is active — harmless when both point at the same proxy, but it inverts the mental model in our docs. Worth a gotcha note in `copilot-claude-proxy.md`, and it means "try the fork on another port via the wrapper" requires `copilot-here off` first.

Want me to migrate `43_copilot_proxy.sh` + docs to the fork (pinned, with the extra quota-saving env and the precedence gotcha documented)?

For the default package, since the original is no longer maintained and the user's intent is to migrate to the fork with dual support as a safety net, I'll propose making the fork the default while keeping the ability to fall back to the original via the environment variable.

For the whoami command, the original has `check-usage` but the fork doesn't—instead it has a `debug` command and exposes a `/usage` endpoint. I'll use the `/usage` endpoint when the proxy is running (with jq for a clean summary), falling back to `debug` to show auth status if the server isn't alive. The rate-limit messaging should also be conditional since that only applies to the original. I'm also considering adding an optional environment variable like `COPILOT_PROXY_EXTRA_QUIET` to control whether extra variables get injected into the copilot-run environment.

For model IDs, the fork README mentions hyphenated format like `claude-opus-4-8`, and the previous conversation confirmed the fork accepts and normalizes those. The current defaults use dotted IDs which should work fine on the fork too, so I'll keep them as-is but note that hyphenated variants are also supported. The docs need updating to reflect the fork as the recommended package, include a dual-support table, note the lack of rate limiting, and clarify that the usage viewer is now bundled locally at `/usage-viewer` instead of pointing to an external URL. There's also a precedence gotcha from the previous chat where shell environment variables don't actually override settings.local.json in Claude Code, which needs to be documented.

I should pin the fork to version 1.13.14 (the latest as of July 1, 2026) and verify the fork's process name contains "copilot-api" so the existing pkill pattern works. For detecting which package flavor is installed, I'll create a helper function that checks if the package name matches the original `copilot-api` exactly (with or without version), otherwise it's a fork. The /v1/models endpoint and auth token path are the same across both, so those don't need changes. Migration is complete, verified live, applied to `~/.config/shell`, and committed as `2655173`.

**What changed in [dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh](dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh):**
- Default package is now `@jeffreycao/copilot-api@1.13.14` (the maintained fork). A new `_copilot_pkg_flavor()` helper detects the exact original `copilot-api` package from `COPILOT_API_PKG`, so rollback is still one env var.
- `copilot-proxy start` only passes `--rate-limit`/`--wait` for the original; the fork gets a plain `start --port`.
- `copilot-proxy whoami` on the fork queries the running proxy's `/usage` endpoint (jq-summarized plan/quota) and falls back to `bunx <pkg> debug` when the proxy is down; the original keeps `check-usage`.
- New opt-in `COPILOT_PROXY_QUIET=1` (default off, per your preference) injects the fork-README quota savers (`CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0`, prompt-suggestion/away-summary off, `DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS=1`) into both `copilot-run` and `copilot-here on`. The keys were added to `_copilot_here_keys`, so `copilot-here off` always removes them regardless of the knob.
- Precedence comments now document the empirical gotcha: `settings.local.json` env beats inherited shell env, so the wrappers can't override an active `copilot-here` pin.

**Docs** ([docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md](docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md)) got the fork/original repo links, updated env table, native `/v1/messages` passthrough explanation, the local `/usage-viewer` dashboard URL, and three new gotchas (env precedence, no rate limiter on the fork, the `context_management` 400 wart from caozhiyuan#305).

**Verification results (all passed):**
- Fork started on 4141 and serves the Claude models; live `/v1/messages` probes confirmed both dotted (`claude-opus-4.8`) and hyphenated (`claude-opus-4-8`) ids work — I noted this in the docs since the fork *lists* hyphenated ids, meaning the dotted defaults in the helpers still work.
- `whoami` printed your enterprise plan/quota via `/usage`.
- Rollback test: `COPILOT_API_PKG=copilot-api@0.7.0` on port 4143 started with `--rate-limit 15 --wait` and stopped cleanly.
- Quiet-env round trip in a scratch repo: `on` with quiet adds the 4 extra keys, `off` (quiet unset) removes the file entirely; `copilot-run` injects them only when quiet is set. Checked under both bash and zsh.
- End-to-end headless `copilot-run claude -p` through the fork returned correctly.

The commit includes this session's SpecStory transcripts and the plan file, staged via the history-hygiene skill with a clean gitleaks scan.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The issue is that Claude Code's model identifier doesn't match what's actually being served—it shows "Opus 4" and displays a retirement warning because the model ID `claude-opus-4.8` isn't in its lookup table, and the HUD incorrectly calculates context usage at over 100% since it assumes 200k context when Copilot actually provides 1M. With the fork now available, there might be a way to update the `/model` endpoint to return the correct model information instead of treating this as purely cosmetic.

The fork's README actually has the answer: it recommends configuring model IDs with hyphens instead of dots—`claude-opus-4-8` rather than `claude-opus-4.8`. Claude Code pattern-matches against model strings and recognizes the hyphenated format through prefix matching, whereas the dotted format fails to match and falls back to the legacy "Opus 4" display. So the fix is straightforward: switch the default model IDs to hyphenated versions like `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-sonnet-5`, and `claude-haiku-4-5`. This way Claude Code will properly recognize the model family, display the correct name, handle the 1M context window appropriately, and enable thinking support.</details></think>
